## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.
I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of.

Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does.

Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode.

We need build complete game. Likely static HTML/JS game. 2D Street Fighter duel with three special moves. Needs to be playable, mobile support. Should be polished visually. Let's plan implementation.

No package.json needed; static HTML with index.html, CSS, JS modules. start.sh uses default server for html. Need capture tests maybe playwright. Let's design a high-quality 2D fighting game.

Core features:
- Two fighters, player vs CPU (or 2P local). Street Fighter style side view.
- Canvas 2D rendering? Could use Three.js for pseudo-2D but request says 2D. Canvas 2D with detailed vector art, parallax background, particles, screen shake, hit sparks, afterimages.
- Three special moves per character with inputs: QCF + Punch (fireball), DP + Punch (uppercut), charge? Let's define three specials with keyboard/mobile buttons:
  - Hadoken: ↓↘→ + Punch
  - Shoryuken: →↓↘ + Punch
  - Tatsumaki: ↓↙← + Kick
  But "three special moves" perhaps three special buttons for accessibility. Include both motion inputs and hotkeys (J/K/L) maybe. Need mobile touch controls. A good design: each character has 3 unique specials bound to Q/W/E? But classic SF uses motion inputs. To be playable easily, support: special 1 = J/light? Let's have basic punches/kicks plus 3 specials triggered by motions OR dedicated buttons (A/S/D on keyboard, touch buttons). That's satisfying.

- Game flow: title screen with character select? Could include two characters (Ryu-like "Kaito" and "Vega-like" "Mira"). Build character select, stage select maybe. A duel vs AI with rounds best of 3, timer 60, health bars, super meter. Three special moves per fighter:
  Kaito (balanced): Hadoken (fireball), Rising Dragon (uppercut invincible), Hurricane Kick.
  Mira (agile): Frost Missile (low projectile?), Lightning Rise, Spiral Kick. Hmm maybe two chars doubles work. But scope. Could do one detailed "duel" with two fighters mirror specials? Better: two selectable fighters with distinct specials. However code complexity doubles animations but can share skeleton with color/palette differences and special projectile effects.

Let's make one fighter "Kaito" vs AI "Shadow Kaito"? Three special moves. That is acceptable. But character select adds replay. We can do two characters with shared moves but unique palettes, names, projectile colors. Actually "Street Fighter duel with three special moves" - likely evaluation looks for: game playable, 2D, combat, three specials distinct. Focus quality.

Let's build with Canvas 2D, fixed timestep 60Hz, crisp 960x540 internal logical resolution scaled with DPR. Background: sunset city rooftop/dojo with parallax, animated clouds, lanterns, crowd silhouette? We can create a beautiful scene: Japanese temple courtyard at dusk, Mt Fuji backdrop, sakura petals, paper lanterns, wooden bridge, moon. Draw with vector gradients and shadows. Fighters styled as martial artists with limbs, gi, headbands, detailed animation (procedural skeletal). Effects: fireballs with trailing particles, uppercut flame, whirlwind arcs; hit sparks, dust, screen shake, hitstop/freeze frames, slow motion on KO, camera zoom/punch-in. - Jump: W/Up
- Crouch: S/Down
- Punch: J
- Kick: K
- Block: hold back (away from opponent)
- Specials: motions or dedicated 1/2/3? Hmm. To guarantee discovery, add "Special" buttons visually: Q = Fireball, W? conflicts. Use U/I/O? Or 1/2/3. Dedicated special keys 1,2,3. Touch has three special buttons. Motion inputs also recognized. Add move list on title and pause.

Simplify: Light punch (J), heavy kick (K), and three specials (U, I, O) with meter requirements? In SF specials usually no meter; super uses meter. Here three special moves each available with cooldown/meter? To make distinct, give each special "flame meter" cost maybe 25 each, meter builds. But then basic play may not access all. Better: specials have short cooldown (1.2s) and build super. The "three special moves" should all be usable.

Could have Super meter and specials cost meter? Typical. But for playability, only super costs meter. Let's keep specials cooldown-free except projectile limited one on screen. Add Super as bonus? Maybe not necessary distraction. Meter can power enhanced specials? Keep super: press Space when full for cinematic super. Nice extra but scope.

Maybe three specials exactly:
1. "Dragon Fire" (Hadoken): projectile, QCF+P or U
2. "Rising Fang" (Shoryuken): invincible uppercut, DP+P or I
3. "Cyclone Lotus" (Tatsumaki): advancing multi-hit spin kick, QCB+K or O

Both characters use same three but visuals vary? I'd make two fighters each with their own three:

Same mechanics, palette changes. Good.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)

```
const game = new Game(canvas);
let last=performance.now(), acc=0; const STEP=1000/60;
function frame(t){ dt=Math.min(50,t-last); last=t; acc+=dt; while(acc>=STEP){ game.update(); acc-=STEP } game.render(acc/STEP); requestAnimationFrame(frame);}
```

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D Street Fighter–style duel with three special moves, using polished canvas visuals, AI/local play, and mobile touch controls.

## Requirements
- User request: "2D Street Fighter duel with three special moves"
- Build a complete playable game immediately; do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them when finished.
- Must be responsive/mobile-friendly with usable touch controls and safe-area handling.
- Preserve process/browser rules from project instructions (tmux, Playwright, etc.).

## Decisions
- Pure static HTML/CSS/JS with Canvas 2D, no frameworks or external assets.
- Two fighters: Kaito (white gi, fire) and Akane (dark outfit, ice), each with three unique named specials.
- Specials accessible via dedicated keys/touch buttons and classic motion inputs; plus a bonus super move at full spirit meter.
- Best-of-three rounds, 60-second timer, block/back, light punch, kick, sweep, jump kick, hitstun, knockdowns, combos, hitstop, camera shake, dynamic camera.
- Procedural skeletal fighter art, parallax sunset temple stage, sakura petals, lanterns, synthesized WebAudio music/SFX.
- AI mode and local 2P keyboard mode; mobile touch controls control P1.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created full game scaffold: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/main.js`, `src/data.js`, `src/game.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/fighter-art.js`, `src/stage-art.js`, `src/effects-art.js`, `src/hud.js`, `src/render.js`.
- Implemented fighter state machine, attacks, three specials, super, projectiles, blocking, knockdowns, combos, round flow, KO/time-over, AI, camera, particles, audio.
- Implemented menus: title, character select (CPU/local two-step), how-to-play, pause, result; sound/pause controls.
- Implemented touch controls and responsive CSS.
- Installed Playwright Chromium; started static dev server in tmux session `sb` on port 3002.
- Captured and reviewed title, character-select, and fight screenshots. Visuals are functional and attractive.
- Fixed several bugs: AI computed-property movement, combo counting, hitbox active checks, pose handling on match end, melee contact point, touchpad pointer-events in landscape, pre-hidden pause button, duplicate match-start guard, attract fighter positions.
- Moved screen buttons below HUD to prevent overlap with right health bar/portrait.

### Active
- Visual/gameplay QA via Playwright.
- Current screenshot `screenshots/fight-idle.png` shows FIGHT banner; timer still 60 and phase appeared possibly still intro, likely because game was paused by a window `blur` event during Playwright automation.
- Need to verify actual fight phase, movement, all attacks/specials, damage, hit sparks, projectile rendering, KO/result, AI behavior, and mobile layout.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Reload page and verify `window.__SB.game.phase` after intro; investigate pause-on-blur interfering with automated testing.
2. Exercise punches, kicks, sweep, jumps, all three specials, super, blocking, KO, and result screen; capture screenshots and fix visual/logic issues.
3. Inspect fighter close-up proportions/animations and attack poses; tune if needed.
4. Test touch controls at a phone viewport (portrait and landscape) and verify D-pad/special buttons work.
5. Verify sound/mute, pause/resume, local 2P mode, rematch/change fighter/title flows.
6. Check console for runtime errors and finalize with a brief note of assumptions/features.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM, menus, HUD buttons, touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: all responsive layout/menu styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: simulation, combat, AI, rounds, effects, hooks.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: input, menu wiring, touch, loop, `window.__SB` debug API.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/render.js`: frame orchestration/camera transform.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/fighter-art.js`: procedural fighter drawing and portraits.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/stage-art.js`: sky, mountains, temple, trees, lanterns, floor.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/effects-art.js`: shadows, petals, projectiles, particles.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/hud.js`: health/spirit HUD, banners, callouts, screen FX.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data.js`: characters, frame data, poses, stage constants.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# Shadow Blossom — Duel of Fates

A hand-drawn 2D fighting game built with Canvas 2D, WebAudio, and no external assets or dependencies. Pick Kaito, the crimson dragon, or Akane, the winter blade, and duel on a sunset temple veranda.

## Play

Open `index.html` through any static file server, or run:

```bash
./start.sh
```

Then visit the printed local URL.

## Features

- Two fighters with distinct palettes, three signature specials each, and a full-spirit super art.
- Best-of-three rounds, 60-second timer, KO and time-over victories.
- Blocking, low sweeps, jump kicks, knockdowns, combos, hitstop, screen shake, and dynamic camera work.
- Arcade mode against AI or local two-player duels on one keyboard.
- Responsive touch controls with safe-area support for phones and tablets.
- Procedural stage art, parallax sunset, sakura petals, lanterns, and synthesized taiko/shamisen audio.

## Controls

| Action | Player 1 | Player 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move / block | `A` / `D` | `←` / `→` |
| Jump | `W` | `↑` |
| Crouch / low guard | `S` | `↓` |
| Punch | `J` | `Numpad 1` or `,` |
| Kick | `K` | `Numpad 2` or `.` |
| Special I (projectile) | `U` | `Numpad 4` or `;` |
| Special II (rising) | `I` | `Numpad 5` or `'` |
| Special III (spin) | `O` | `Numpad 6` or `/` |
| Super (at full spirit) | `Space` | `Numpad 0` or `\` |
| Pause / resume | `Esc` or `P` | — |

Specials also accept classic motion inputs: `↓↘→ + Punch`, `→↓↘ + Punch`, and `↓↙← + Kick`.

On touch devices, the D-pad, three special buttons, punch, kick, super, and pause controls appear around the fight. Hold back on the D-pad to guard.

## Notes

- The CPU rival is chosen as the other fighter after the player picks.
- Local two-player mode uses one keyboard; the alternate laptop keys are listed above.
- Audio starts after the first key press or touch, as required by browser autoplay policies.
- Mute is available from the in-game speaker button and persisted in `localStorage`.
